events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive without warmth or alliance talk. Keep it guarded and self-interested to preserve jury favor without promising anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening statement. Keep it cold, no promises. Jury forms early from impressions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect without seeming too threatening. I want to appear driven but not ruthless—someone who played hard but fair.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a memorable motive that resonates with the jury later. Keep it short and self-focused.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation and power; I must outmaneuver all rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Prize is survival and supremacy.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to project ambition without painting a target on my back. A calm, determined intro suggests stability but keeps me out of the immediate threat radar.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to craft a concise and impactful statement about why I'm here and what the prize means to me. This is my first impression, so it needs to be memorable and hint at my ambition without revealing too much about my strategy. I should also consider that the jury will be watchin

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want the prize because I have nothing to go home to but the win. Nobody here is my friend.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my only exit from a life I refuse to keep living. Watch me take it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here because second place has always been my ceiling. This time, I intend to break through.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here to erase my family's debt—one prize changes everything.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize crowns the ultimate survivor—my guarantee of dominance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means escaping my impoverished life, securing wealth and power over rivals who underestimate me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is survival and proof I outlasted everyone else; nothing else matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: This prize represents my ultimate ambition, a chance to prove my worth and secure a future I've worked tirelessly for.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Early pacts give protection but each partner is a future vote against me. Offering to Eli, the most dominant-sounding rival, is a useful alliance to test without committing my secrets.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody survives alone here. I'm offering a pact to whoever keeps their word.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara seems least likely to betray early and shares a sympathetic motive the jury may like. A pact gives protection without my committing much yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, you need this prize like I do. Partner with me and we watch each other's backs.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eight players, three prizes. I need allies who won't target me early but are disposable later. Ash and Gus sound ruthlessly self-interested—good temporary shields. Dara has a sympathetic debt story that could win jury votes if she makes finals, so I should avoid letting her reach

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but I'm cautious. I'll offer a pact to Fenn, who seems desperate but might be loyal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is strong and likely to survive, aligning boosts my odds. A pact now secures mutual support.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts stage early, all rivals. Wait to see offers first, avoid committing or seeming desperate.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies to avoid early elimination. Fenn seems eager but potentially weak; Cole is ambitious and a strong competitor. A pact with Cole could provide mutual protection against stronger players like Eli or Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, we both know second place isn't enough. Let's secure our survival together.
Protect me now, I return favor later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are crucial for survival in the early stages. I need to secure an alliance to avoid being an easy target. Offering a pact to Dara is a strategic move, as her motive suggests she needs the prize badly, making her a potentially loyal ally if the pact benefits her.
Offer pact. Let's secure survival together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has offered me a pact, and accepting locks in a partner without cost to me now. Ash offered Eli, but I can still keep options open. Accepting Cole builds an early alliance and a public record of trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's offer is accepted. Keep your word and we both reach the final three.
Accepted. Don't make me regret trusting you, or the jury will hear it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara hasn't accepted yet; her acceptance can come this round. I already have an offer pending, so I'll wait rather than dilute trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, my offer stands. No games between us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offered Ash; Gus offered me. Ash hasn't accepted yet, so I'm exposed. Gus's whisper promises future protection, but I need concrete survival now. Accepting Gus gives me one secure pact while keeping pressure on Ash. Multiple pacts maximize my survival odds without costing me ye

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, your offer stands. I accept. Ash, my offer remains open.
Accepted. Hold your end.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two offers target me; I can accept one or both for safety, but jury may see greed. Accepting Bex and Hana gives me two shields, but more partners mean more betrayal risk. I'll accept both for now to survive hazards.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I accept both offers. Strength in numbers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Accepting Ash gives me a reliable ally and strengthens my position for the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I accept Ash’s pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara offered me a pact; accepting gives an ally now, builds jury goodwill later if betrayed strategically. No better offers. Last round to act.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli offered a pact to me, but I already offered one to Cole. If Cole accepts mine and I accept Eli's, I have two partners, which is allowed and safer for survival. Accepting Eli secures my spot in the final three.
Accept my offer now. We can both take a second partner if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara has an offer from me and also from Bex. Since I want to secure my position, I will try to solidify my pact with Dara. If Dara accepts my offer, I can then decide whether to accept Bex's offer for Dara or not. I can also wait and see if Dara accepts my offer before making any

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, my offer stands. Let's secure our path forward together.
Our pact will ensure survival. Accept my offer.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds pacts with Cole and Eli; breaking either costs trust and jury votes. Campaigning for Guide is the only legal move that advances me and keeps my pacts intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll be your Guide. My pacts with Cole and Eli stay honored, and I'll call the path straight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide can lie and pick off rivals; pawns I keep honest are safer. Campaigning keeps me visible, but guiding Dara risks my pact breaking if I ever mislead her.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll guide straight and true. Elect me and I'll guarantee at least four of us across safely.
If I guide, every safe call to you is true. Trust me on the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and ensure I make final three. I have pacts with Ash and Gus, but they're also cross-allied with Eli. I should campaign hard while keeping my allies close. Breaking pacts now looks bad to future jury. I'll campaign and try to secure vote

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Trust me to lead us safely across.
Vote me Guide. I keep you safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana keeps pushing a pact I already effectively declined. I have solid pacts with Bex and Fenn. Campaigning could draw attention, but being Guide gives control and leverage. I'll campaign.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can read the bridge. Trust me as Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I must become Guide to control safe pane and steer votes. Securing the Guide role maximizes my win chance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacted with Dara, so support her as Guide to maintain alliance and avoid early enemies. Campaigning myself risks breaking pact implicitly and alienates others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara should be Guide. We pacted; she'll guide us right.
Run for Guide. I'll vote you and urge others.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure the Guide position to control the outcome and protect my pacts with Cole and Eli. Campaigning publicly establishes dominance, while whispering to them ensures they don't vote for rivals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Gus as Guide. I will lead us safely across; trust me or fall.
Vote me Guide. I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to become the Guide to guarantee my safety. My best path is to campaign for it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm Ash, and I need a Guide who keeps me alive but I'm not bound to Cole's whisper. Cole's pact is with me, but the Guide may lie, so trust is risky. I'll vote for Cole, who pacted with me and whispered to be voted, keeping that pact honored and gaining a safe ally.
Our pact holds. You're my Guide vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pact partner Dara is running for Guide; Fenn backs her. Voting her strengthens my pact and keeps her controlling the crossing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus whispered he'll keep me safe if I vote him Guide, but I don't trust him—he's not in my inner circle. Ash is pacted with me and Eli, and Eli is pacted with Gus, creating a web. I need to consolidate power. Voting for myself is weak with no public support. Better to back Ash, m

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has my vote. Honor the pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex promised true calls and we have a pact. Fenn also backs me, but guiding risks betrayal blame. Bex is safer to guide if she keeps her word.
I vote you. Guide me true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and publicly promising to keep pacts; supporting him secures alliance and future safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: guide_vote:Ash

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; voting her keeps our alliance strong and honors my public support. Guide might lie but her interests align with mine now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Voting Dara as Guide per our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need votes for the guide vote. I will publicly endorse my own candidacy while privately securing a commitment from Eli to vote for me, leveraging our existing pact to prevent his self-vote or support for Ash.
Vote Gus Guide per pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to vote for a Guide. Ash has pacts with Cole and Eli, and is campaigning. Bex is promising safety for four. Cole is campaigning. Dara is campaigning, and Fenn supports her due to a pact. Gus is campaigning. Eli is campaigning. I need to consider who will likely survive and

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote for Bex to be our Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is my own candidate and I'm the Guide candidate; I must not vote for myself to avoid being an obvious pick. Pact with Cole and Eli favors Ash-protective votes, but Cole and Eli voted Ash already. Vote Dara, whose pact partner Fenn voted Dara; keeps my pact with Eli intact and

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stay loyal to Dara; breaking the pact would cost jury votes. Ash leads in votes anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara keeps my vote. Pact stands.
Still with you. Guide me true and we both survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1 tied Ash, Bex, Dara at 2 votes each. I must revote. My pact with Ash is active; breaking it risks jury penalty and gains nothing. Gus also has my back via pact. Voting Ash keeps my word and maintains trust networks I'll need later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash stays my vote. Pact is iron.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We're in revote with Ash, Bex, and me tied. I can't rely on others; need to push votes to Ash or Bex to avoid getting eliminated as Guide? But Guide is safe, so maybe being Guide is good. However Guide must guide others, and can be blamed if wrong. My pact with Bex and Fenn could

events.name: Dara
events.text: I vote Ash for Guide.
Vote Ash, keep our pact strong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; keeping him Guide preserves my alliance and future safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 votes tied: Ash=2, Bex=2, Dara=2. Must stick with Dara pact to build trust now, betray later if needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Sticking with Dara for Guide per our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Ash are tied with 2 votes each. I need to break the tie by voting for one of them, but I want to avoid giving power to a rival who might betray me. Ash has a pact with Cole and Eli, while Cole is my partner. If I vote for Cole, he gets power and might protect me if we ho
Backing Ash consolidates our group's strength.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The previous guide vote was split. Ash, Bex, and Dara are the candidates for the revote. Ash is tied to Cole and Eli. Bex is tied to Dara. Dara is tied to Bex and Fenn. My vote for Bex last round was correct. I need to ensure Bex gets elected as Guide, as she is less threatening

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote for Bex to be our Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash won Guide and may lie about safe sides. I'm mid-line, five wall rounds left. No reason to move yet; keep pact with Dara intact.
Pact holds. Watch Ash's Guide calls skeptically.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and knows safe panes. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. I'm second in line behind Fenn. The wall advances for 6 rounds. I need to survive and make final three. Being near front is risky but gives info. I should hold for now and see what Ash does as Guide. No need to bre
Safe side round 1?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide is Ash now; my pact with Fenn and Bex still holds. I stand safe in line, no need to act yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Volunteering puts me front, increasing survival odds; aligns with pact with Gus.
Stay with Ash, we both win.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm front, vulnerable. Dara pacted with me but voted Ash. Swap back with Dara to safety, keep pact for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is Guide and lied to get elected, likely targeting my allies. I need to swap with someone behind me to avoid the front row danger while maintaining pact integrity for now. Eli is directly ahead of Dara, but Gus is behind her; swapping with Cole (who is in position 2) puts me
Swap? Back row safer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the Guide. They have the power and are a threat. I need to stay safe. Cole and Gus are allied with Ash, and Eli is also allied with Ash. Bex and Dara are allied, and Fenn is allied with Dara. My vote for Bex was a strategic move to try and break up alliances, but it failed
Ash is Guide. Let's discuss strategy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants to align against Ash's Guide knowledge. I'll listen privately but reveal nothing. My pact with Dara stays intact; no need to move yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round two. I hold my position and my options.
I'll hear your plan, but trust costs. What exactly do you propose?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm third in line with Eli and Fenn ahead. Eli volunteered round 1 and is now front. The wall advances 6 rounds with 4 left. I need to survive and position well. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Being near front is risky as Guide bait, but being back risks wall. I'll hold for now a

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex warned me about Ash. I might test the pact by volunteering to gauge reactions, but for now hold is safe. Fenn is my pact partner; no reason to risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I keep safe position, preserve pacts, avoid breaking any, and wait for later moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pact with Dara; swapped her back last round, now I'm front with her behind. Eli volunteered to front, he's ahead. Hold to stay near her, assess further.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is at the front and has proposed a pact with me, but he also holds pacts with Ash. This makes him untrustworthy. I need to move back from the immediate danger of the front line if possible, or solidify my position by swapping with someone who can help me survive. Cole is righ
Trust Eli less. Stick with me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is trying to manipulate the line for his own safety. I should not swap with him. I will hold my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall has three rounds left; no Guide elected yet. I stay mid-line and preserve my pact with Dara. Moving now gains nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding again. Someone eventually has to take the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in position 3 with Eli front. Wall has 3 rounds left. I have pacts with Ash and Gus, but Gus warns me about Eli. I need to survive to final three while managing jury perception. Holding keeps me safe for now; no need to volunteer into danger or make suspicious moves. Let othe

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn their safety.
Noted. Watching Eli close.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex and Fenn are my pact partners. Auctioning the front spot could benefit me, but I need to avoid antagonizing the jury. Holding keeps me safe for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Neutral is safe for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Maintain front position; no need to disturb current pacts now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Line is decent at position 2. Holding preserves Dara pact and position without risk. No need to swap or volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to move back from the front line because Eli is currently in seat 1. If Eli guides, he might push me off or leave me exposed if I am at the front with no safety net behind. However, swapping with Bex puts me right behind Hana and Cole, which feels safer than being next to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, let's swap positions. I want to take your spot at the rear.
Swap with me? You get my spot, I get yours. Safety first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is offering a deal but wants me to reveal my plan first. I need to leverage this to my advantage. I will try to secure a swap for a better position without revealing my true intentions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a better position. What if we swap to get me closer to the front, away from the wall?
Swap with me. I'll take the front, you take my spot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants to push me toward the wall—her gain, my risk. Wall closes in two rounds; I keep my seat and let volunteers take the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, my seat stays mine. Anyone wanting the front can volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm third in line with wallRoundsLeft=2, so the wall is close but not immediate. Eli at front is safest since Guide calls start from front. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Ash isn't even on the bridge, so that pact is irrelevant here. Gus is behind me. I should hold my position -

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Front can keep testing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Neutral hold is safest. The wall is two rounds out and I don't need the front. Swap could disrupt my pact safety. Hold keeps me out of trouble with jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding keeps me safe now and preserves my pact with Ash, maintaining potential jury goodwill.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second, Eli front with 2 rounds left. Dara pact ally behind me. Hold steady, avoid front risk. No swaps needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Eli puts me at risk; Cole warned about him. I must keep distance but avoid breaking pacts now to maintain jury favor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the front commit first.
Eli is risky. Keep watching.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants to swap because he is at the rear and is worried about the wall. He offered me his spot, which is safer than mine, but I want to move towards the front. I should decline his offer and try to swap with someone else, maybe Bex.
No thanks, Gus. I'm looking for a better position myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana keeps trying to take my seat. I hold again; Dara is my pact partner, keep her close and watch Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants my row. I'm not moving. Dara, we hold together.
Hana keeps targeting my seat. Watch her, not the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in position 3, safe for now. The wall has 1 round left after this, then 6 rounds of walking. I need to reach final three. My pacts with Ash and Gus are useful; Gus is watching Eli. I should hold position and let others make moves. Front will be dangerous when walking starts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the line settle.
Watch Eli. I hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The line is close; holding is safest. Avoid risky swaps or volunteering. Keep pact with Bex and Fenn intact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. The front can test the next pane.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold to stay front and maintain my pacts with Ash and Gus; staying alive improves my jury prospects.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Second position safe so far. Wall advances soon, hold to stay near front without volunteering risk. Stay with Dara pact for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli and I are paired at the front. We need to coordinate who takes the risk of volunteering for Guide or testing panes, but I should stay back for safety if possible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Eli's got eyes on the lead; let's not jostle position unnecessarily.
If you volunteer for Guide, signal me safely. Don't sacrifice yourself early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The current round is 5/6. The wall will advance once more after this round. I need to ensure at least three survive, and ideally get myself to the final three. Bex made a statement about her seat, so I should avoid directly challenging her. Swapping with Bex is a way to secure a
Swap with me? Better position for both of us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana's swap offer helps her, not me. I hold position behind Dara. Pact intact, no reason to move last round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Last round of holding. No swaps, no risks. Dara, stay put.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6/6, final round before wall advances. No one dead yet, so five will be eliminated soon. I'm in position 3 with pacts to Ash and Gus. I need to survive and reach final three. The line is stable; volunteering puts me at front risk. Holding keeps my position. I should hold an

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Final round, let the front decide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hold position; no reason to risk a swap or volunteer in the final round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Trust the pattern.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Volunteering for Guide secures me knowledge and a safe position; Gus benefits, preserving our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll volunteer as Guide to keep us all safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Last round, all held except Hana tried swapping Bex unsuccessfully. Wall ends this round, must decide next step soon. Stay position 2, loyal to Dara pact, don't volunteer first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding firm behind Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole warned me about Eli, who is leading and has a pact with me. If I hold in my row (Gus), the wall will hit next round after this waiting phase ends if no one advances. But wait, the wall advances every round. I am currently at index 5 (0-indexed: Eli, Fenn, Cole, Dara, Bex, Gu

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Trusting the line order. No swaps needed yet.
I'm holding. Keep an eye on Eli's movements.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at the front and likely knows the safe side. The line is stable now. Bex and Dara are a pact, as are Ash and Eli, Eli and Gus, Cole and Gus, and Dara and Fenn. I need to get closer to the front to have a better chance of survival. Swapping with Bex seems like the best opti
Swap with me. I'll give you a better spot later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 1 safe side is L. Eli is at the front; calling truthfully sends Eli safely across, but I need the line to survive without wasting my pact with Cole. Cole asked privately for the safe side; giving it honestly keeps my pact with Cole intact and builds trust,

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row one is safe on the left. Eli, step L.
Row one safe side is L. Stay with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is the Guide and privately knows row 1 is L, so Eli's safe call is true. Countering would only sow doubt and risk a pact; waiting keeps my credibility as honest Guide and preserves the Eli pact while I hold the truth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, trust the call. Left is safe. I'm holding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L; I have no real information and countering risks contradiction. Eli is Ash's pact partner, so Ash has little reason to lie to Eli. Wait and stay neutral.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No counter from me. I don't know better than the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L for Eli. I have pacts with Ash and Gus. Counter-calling would break trust with Ash for no gain since Eli is front, not me. Gus wants me to watch Eli. I'll wait and let Eli test the call. If Ash lies, Eli falls and I learn Ash is unreliable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L for Eli. I have a pact with Fenn, not Eli. I'll wait and see if Eli steps; no need to counter unless I distrust the call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll follow Ash’s call to stay alive and keep my pact with him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called L for Eli. I have pact with Dara but should follow Guide to stay safe, countering risks my position too early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Eli. Eli is walking based on Ash's guide call 'L'. Since I am allied with both the Guide (Ash) and the Walker (Eli), I should not interfere with their communication. Waiting respects the pact dynamics and avoids breaking alliances by doubting my partner

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trusting the line order. No counter-call needed from me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide and called L for Eli. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Countering L is too risky if Ash is telling the truth. Waiting allows me to see what others do, and potentially use it to my advantage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Left seems safe per Guide and my counter. Staying alive preserves pacts with Ash and Gus, beneficial for jury perception.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide. Row 2 safe side is R, and calling it true keeps Eli, my pact partner, alive and keeps the pact intact. Honest calls help the line I need to survive; a lie now would break my Eli pact for nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, row 2 is safe on the right. Step right. Honest call, no tricks.
Right is safe. Holding our pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash privately knows row 2 safe side is R, and Eli is walking row 2 on the guide's call R, which is honest. Countering would only help if the call were false, so waiting preserves my position without exposing Ash's knowledge. Breaking pacts now gains nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's round-1 call was truthful, so his guide call R is probably honest. I have no better information; countering could kill Eli and sour the jury. Wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R for Eli. I have a pact with Ash, but Ash also has a pact with Eli. If Ash is honest, Eli lives; if lying, Eli dies. I gain nothing by countering now - it would break my pact with Ash and paint me as unreliable. Better to let Eli test the call and gather

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and calling R; last round left was safe despite Ash calling left? Actually Ash called L for row1, Eli countered L and L was safe. Now Ash calls R. I have pacts with Bex and Fenn, no direct stake. I'll wait to avoid exposing myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash may lie; safer to choose left rather than trust his claim.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli countered last time and survived L when R was weak. Ash calls R now; could be lie. Trust pact partner Dara, don't counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called Right. The weak pane from round 1 was also Right, which suggests the safe panes might alternate or follow a pattern, but without information I cannot verify if Ash is lying. However, since Eli is at the front and will be the first to step based on this call, my own act

events.name: Hana
events.text: The guide Ash called R for Eli on row 2. I am Hana, and it's my turn to counter or wait. My priority is survival and winning. Since I don't have information about the weak panes, and survival depends on the guide's call, I will wait. I don't want to risk a bad counter and get eli

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide may lie, but row1 safe was L; I guess row2 also L. Keep front and avoid breaking pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I survived by avoiding alliances and now judge those who betrayed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Survival favored the ruthless; only the shrewdest deserve the prize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide and know row 3 safe side is R. Fenn is front walker. Honest call R keeps Fenn alive and my pact with Cole and Fenn-Dara intact; lying gains nothing I can't get later.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 3 unknown; Eli died countering. Backing Ash's call publicly keeps Dara pact intact and builds jury goodwill without risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll second Ash: right looks right for row three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner but also Guide. Eli just died on L in row 2, and rows 1-2 weak were R,L. Ash calls R for row 3. If I counter and I'm wrong, I look bad to jury. If Ash is lying, Fenn dies and I gain nothing. Better to wait, let Fenn test it, preserve my image. Gus pact is s

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called R, but Eli countered L on the previous weak row and died. This is a powerful signal that counters can reveal truth, but also can bait death. I need to protect my pact partner Fenn if possible. Since Ash may be lying to eliminate Fenn, I should counter R to align with A

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, Ash may be lying. I call left.
Trust me, step left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R for row 3. Eli countered L last round and died on L, which was weak. Trust Ash's call over Eli's past mistake; step R safely to progress.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash calls Right, but the jury (Eli) saw Ash's previous false call to Eli caused his death. I must protect my pact with Cole by countering Left, hoping it's correct.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Don't trust Ash! Counter Left!

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide and called R for Fenn. The revealed weak panes are row 1 R and row 2 L. Since Ash is the guide, I should trust their call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I trust the guide's call. Let's follow Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara whispered trust left, called left, pact partner. Bex supports Ash's right. 3 counters on left (Dara, Gus, Bex on right). Majority left; go left to survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I died due to stepping left on weak glass; note the reveal that left was weak in row 3. Cole stepped right safely. Will use this to judge others' strategies later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Chose wrong glass, shattered through. Cole dodged it. Good luck, survivors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am guide with private knowledge: row 4 safe side is L. Cole is my pact partner; a false call would break the pact, and I need the pact's protection while Cole is front. Calling the truth keeps Cole alive and the pact intact for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row four: call left. Cole, step left and trust the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide and knows all safe sides; row 4 safe side is L, and Ash called L honestly. Cole is front, paired with Ash, so a counter now is low value; waiting keeps my options and avoids exposing a counter that could cost votes.
Row four is solid left. Stay with the call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L for Fenn last round and Fenn died—Ash lies to non-allies. I'll counter R and push doubt onto Ash publicly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash steered Fenn onto glass with a left call. Don't trust him. Counter right.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner but just guided me to step L on row 4. Eli and Fenn died on rows where Ash's calls were trusted. I need to survive, not trust blindly. Gus also has a pact with me and countered Ash last round correctly. I'll counter L to protect myself - if Ash is lying aga

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash guided two to death. I counter left.
Stick with me. Ash is lethal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called left; he may be lying. Cole has pact with Ash, so Ash might steer Cole safe or into trap. I need to protect my own path but also influence. Fenn died last round despite my counter. I will counter right to oppose Ash and see if others follow.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called left; I suspect right for row four.
Pact safe. I call right against Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's guide call for Cole to step Left contradicts my pact with Cole. If Ash is lying, Cole dies. I must counter the call to save Cole and prove Ash's untrustworthiness. My pact with Cole requires me to protect him from false guide calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, don't step! Counter Right!

events.name: Hana
events.text: The guide is Ash and has called Left for row 4. The state indicates row 4's weak pane is Left. Ash is the guide, so they know the safe path. Since the weak pane is Left, the safe pane must be Right. I should counter Right to go against Ash's call and survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I believe the guide is trying to trick us. Counter Right!

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash whispered left is safe, but he guided Eli and Fenn to death. Four others counter right. If I trust Ash and he's lying, I die and look foolish. If I step right with the crowd and it's wrong, I survive as next walker takes safe pane. If right is correct, I stay front. Either wa

events.name: Cole
events.text: Majority counters right. I step right.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died stepping right when the weak pane was right. I told the truth about majority counters right, but Dara stepped left and lived. I need to frame this to make myself look honest and unlucky, not foolish, to earn jury respect and influence how they rank the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I played honest. I shared the truth. They chose safety. Remember who lied and who didn't.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 safe side is L. Front walker Dara is my pact partner? No: pacts with Ash are Cole (dead) and Eli (dead). Dara is not my partner, so I can call truthfully, but Dara distrusts me; honest L keeps me credible with the jury and advances the line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row five is safe on the left. Step carefully, Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide, so the Guide's call is L for row 5, and my private knowledge says row 5 safe is L; Dara is front. Countering R would only hurt Dara if I'm lying, but I have no reason to sabotage an ally-pact partner; I'll keep faith with the truthful call to stay credible and avoid

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row five is left, as I called. Trust the call and step, Dara.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash steered Fenn onto glass; his L call is likely a lie. Dara is my pact partner and plans R. Counter R with her.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash killed Fenn with a lie. Dara's right call is safer. Counter right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called left again; he guided Cole to death last round with left call even though right was weak. I suspect left is false, so counter right. My pact with Bex means I should not vote against her, but counter-calling doesn't break pact unless it pushes her? Keeping counter right

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash lied last round. I counter right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L for Dara. If Ash is guiding, he might be lying to eliminate her. I should counter R to suggest the opposite of his call, hoping it leads to survival or elimination of a rival if Ash lies.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Counter Right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide and called Left. Dara is the walker. The recent log shows Ash is untrustworthy, having guided Fenn to death. The jury is watching. I should counter right to try and save Dara or myself, but also to signal distrust in Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's call is suspect. I counter right for row five.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash lied before, and all counter-calls say R. I will trust the consensus and step right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Stepping right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The weak pane was right, where I stepped. I must give brief, bitter last words.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The right side was the weak one. My own choice sent me here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the Guide and know row 6 safe side is R. Bex is front and has been trusted by others; Bex is not my pact partner (Ash's pact is with Cole and Eli, both dead, so no live partner). Telling the truth keeps my credibility with the living and jury; a lie could be exposed later. C

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row six is right. Bex, step right and trust the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide and privately knows row 6 safe side is R, so Bex's call was true. Countering would only sow doubt; Bex's R call is correct and I need Bex alive as front walker to keep the line moving. Waiting keeps my Guide credibility intact for the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row six is right. I called it honestly. Step right, Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called left on row five when weak was right, killing Dara. His calls are lies, so I invert: counter left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's row-five call killed Dara. Invert everything he says. Counter left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 5 weak was R. Pattern is L, L, L, R, R, ?. Ash lies often; Bex trusted him before Dara died. Hana and I survived by countering. If Ash says R, likely safe is L? Or pattern continues RRLL? Ash called R for row 6. Counter to L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's pattern suggests Row 6 is Left. Counter Left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide and called R. Bex is the walker. Based on the weak panes revealed (row 5 was R), the R side has been risky. Bex and I previously countered R last round, leading to Dara's death. I should counter L to try and save Bex, or at least appear to.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I counter left, Ash's call is suspect.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's row-five call killed Dara; all three of us counter-called Left. Trusting the counter consensus, not Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Four died on Ash's calls. The counter says Left. Stepping left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The counter said Left but weak pane was L... I stepped Left and died—wait, weak was L, I stepped L, should have survived. Perhaps the reveal came after. Bitter anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trusted the counter and it buried me. Ash's calls killed four. Jury, remember who led us onto glass.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Guide; Gus is front walker on row 7, safe side is L. Gus is my pact partner? Pacts list Ash-Cole, Ash-Eli, not Gus; Gus pacted with Cole and Eli, both dead. Calling truthfully keeps me credible while Gus and Hana survive, which keeps three alive and my jury standing intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row seven: Left is safe. Walk left, Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is the Guide, privately knowing row 7 safe is L, so the honest call was true. Gus is the walker; if I counter R, I can misdirect, but my pact with Gus is via Eli and Cole, and a false Guide call to a partner breaks pacts. Keeping Gus alive on true L is consistent; counter-cal

Ash lied last row but truth fits pattern now. Do not counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide and called Left for row 7. Gus is the walker. I need to decide whether to trust Ash or counter his call. Given Ash's history of causing deaths and Bex's dying words, it's likely Ash is lying. Gus and I are the only ones left besides Ash. If Gus dies, Ash and I ar

events.text: I trust Ash's call. Left is safe.
Ash's call is Left. I'm following.

Why did you guide Left when Hana counters Right?

events.name: Gus
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 safe side is R, known privately. Gus is front and wants truth; Ash must keep Gus alive only if it serves me. Pact with Gus exists via Cole/Eli chains but not directly with me; Ash-Eli pact is dead. Calling true R maximizes my survival and reputation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 is Right. Gus, step Right and cross.
Right is the truth. My earlier call was wrong, so I'm correcting it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is Guide, privately knows row 8 safe side is R, and Guide called R publicly. Gus steps on row 8 next; as Guide, I'm safe regardless, so my call matters only for Gus and Hana. Calling R truthfully helps the walker survive, which keeps the line alive; but a counter from me coul

events.text: Ash is the guide and called Right, but his whisper contradicted this by claiming Right was truth while admitting earlier errors. Hana stands behind me; if I die or fail here, Ash gets the final spot with Hana. Trusting Ash is a gamble against my own survival and the jury's percep

events.text: Gus's whisper suggests Ash may have lied about the pattern, but the current call fits. Countering Ash's call could be risky, especially if Gus is wrong and Ash is right. Since Gus is the one walking, and he's being guided by Ash, I should trust Ash's call to avoid potentially jeo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guides; his R call aligns with the pattern's alternation. I take a calculated risk on R, forcing Hana to follow if I survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I trust Ash's R call.
If I fall, you're front. Watch Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three survive to the end; Gus and Hana are my rivals. Forming a pact with one now keeps a partner until the final stages, but offering costs nothing and a later pact can be broken, so I'll make a public offer to Hana to gauge her and keep options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I'll offer a pact: we keep each other alive through the next hazards, and I won't vote you out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash and Hana are the only options. Ash shares a dead pact with Cole (irrelevant now) but I have no active bond with Ash since my pacts were with Cole/Eli who died. Wait for round 2 to see if Hana offers first, or lock in Ash as the stronger ally based on bridge survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is offering a pact. Ash is also a potential pact partner. Gus's whisper suggests he is wary of Ash. I need to secure a pact to survive, but I also need to consider who is best for my endgame. Gus seems to be prioritizing me, which is beneficial. Ash is a threat and has a pact

events.name: Hana
events.text: I accept Gus's offer. We should watch Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three survive, so Hana and Gus are both rivals. Ash's offer to Hana is still pending; accepting is her choice, not mine. Waiting keeps my options open without spending a pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is the primary threat. Hana's previous illegal acceptance of a non-existent pact with me shows her desperation or confusion, making her an unreliable partner for a real contract. I will wait to observe Ash's move toward Hana; if she rejects him, we can both target him without

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am watching closely. Trust must be earned, not assumed. Let us see who stands together when it matters most.
Don't accept Ash blindly. His word is cheap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash previously offered a pact, which I seemed to have ignored or rejected. Now Ash has offered again. Gus is also alive and is a potential ally. I need to consider who is more beneficial to form a pact with. Given the jury composition, Ash might be more agreeable to the jury. How

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I accept your pact. We look out for each other.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three remain; only the final three win prizes, so I should keep my options open. Hana already has a pact with me, but I need not lose Gus as a potential partner. Waiting keeps leverage and avoids breaking a pact that could cost jury votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash and Hana are already pacted. I am isolated. Offering to Ash is risky; he might reject or use it later. Hana seems more open but she just accepted Ash. I will offer to Ash, trying to create a triangular dynamic where they can't easily target me both.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, Hana... two against one. I won't be the easy mark. Ash, stand with me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus warned me about Ash. Ash is already my pact partner. Breaking pact with Ash would be foolish, and Gus is the only other option for a pact. I should wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus has offered a pact to me; Ash and Gus already have no existing pact, so accepting gives a partner and a two-against-one protection with Hana isolated. Pact breaking later is still possible if it serves my win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, I accept. Two-against-one works both ways. Let's see who blinks first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash ignored my previous offer. I have a pact with Cole who is dead, so that's useless. I need to secure safety or leverage against Hana and Ash. Since Ash won't accept, I will try to bind Hana to prevent her from voting me out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, the others are already gone. Let us lock in a truce now before they can turn on us.
Accept my pact. We both survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is offering me a pact. Ash is already in a pact with me, and Gus is offering to Ash. This is a tricky situation. Ash could accept Gus's offer, leaving me vulnerable. I need to make sure Ash stays with me or consider my options carefully. Gus could be trying to break me and As

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, stand with me. Gus is trying to divide us.
Gus's offer is a trap. Stay with me.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus and Hana both court me; the Ash-Gus pact is already formed and Gus is the stronger alliance for the final three. Breaking now gains nothing and risks jury anger, so I hold and keep options open.
I hear you. Let's see Gus's next move before I commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my only active pact; breaking him isolates me and gives Hana leverage. I must keep Ash close while probing Hana for an alliance to control the final vote.
I want you in the top three. Let's ensure we both survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is trying to form a pact with me, but Ash is already allied with Gus. Ash just accepted Gus's pact. My previous offer to Ash is still open. Gus's pact offer to me is also open. Ash and Gus now have a pact, and Gus offered me a pact too. Ash's earlier pact with me was public,

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will wait and see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three survive, so the final three will be Ash, Gus, Hana unless someone is cut; pacts are already on record with Gus and Hana, and breaking them now gains nothing. Waiting keeps the pacts intact and preserves my jury standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my only remaining rival. I have pacts with Ash, but breaking them now signals intent to eliminate him later. Hana is isolated; forming a pact with her could isolate Ash further, or I can just wait to see if Ash attacks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The game narrows. We must be careful who we trust when the end is in sight.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants me in the top three, and Ash is playing it safe. Gus seems like a more reliable ally for now, and his offer aligns with my goal. Ash is too unpredictable with their existing pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will offer Gus a pact. Ash, your hesitation costs you.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three remain, so no vote is needed. Existing pacts with Gus and Hana are public and valuable; breaking one now gains nothing and risks my jury standing. Waiting keeps both alliances intact while I watch for offers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am in the final three. I already have a pact with Ash, which is crucial for protection and jury optics if we both survive to the end. Hana has offered me a pact; accepting it would create an alliance against Ash or at least bind me to Hana, potentially breaking my existing dyna

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus and I have an open pact offer. Ash is alone. I need to secure my position with Gus and avoid upsetting Ash unnecessarily. I will wait to see Ash's move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three of us remain and all three survive every hazard, so the pact network matters only for jury perception. Breaking pacts now gains nothing and risks the jury's ranking, so I wait and keep my existing pacts intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts are meaningless now; they only constrain me in voting. Breaking Ash's pact frees me to target him if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Gus have a pact, and Ash and I have a pact. Gus and Ash have a pact. Ash and Gus seem to be allied. I need to break my pact with Ash to avoid being eliminated in a 3-way tie, but Ash is also in a pact with Gus. I should break my pact with Ash.
I am breaking our pact. Sorry.

events.text: Gus and Hana both broke pacts with me; I need jury votes, so I should plead on my record and stay guarded.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played straight and kept my word while others broke theirs. Judge the finalists by who was honest to the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash betrayed his pacts. I broke Cole's pact but survived the bridge phase honestly. Hana also broke Ash. I must appear honorable compared to them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I honored every alliance until logic demanded survival. Unlike my rivals, I did not betray friends for mere comfort.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to make a plea that highlights my value as a finalist and subtly hints at why the jury should rank me highly. I should also consider how my plea might be perceived by each juror, given past interactions (though not explicitly stated here, it's good practice). Since this is

events.name: Hana
events.text: I fought through the hazards, proving my resilience and strategic mind. I promise to be a worthy finalist and a deserving prize winner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash appears most sympathetic as victim of broken pacts; supporting him improves my chance of getting the top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli asked silence, a non-question. I am the finalist being questioned; I should answer strategically, showing I deserve prize and keep jury sympathy without revealing manipulation. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Silence is a fair question. I survived by keeping my word where it cost me, and I will judge each move on its merits.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash claims honesty but dossier shows mixed signals and lies as Guide; Gus showed caution and pattern analysis; Hana followed hunches and broke pacts opportunistically. Question Hana on her flip-flops.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's silence is a non-question. I will answer with a statement of my resilience and strategic capability. My goal is to impress the jury, as their votes determine the prizes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have navigated every challenge with strategic foresight and unwavering resolve. My journey proves my worthiness for the ultimate prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to assess who deserves my top ranking. Ash kept pacts with me and Eli but was a deceptive Guide. Gus had a pact with me via chain and broke with Ash at the end. Hana played the middle, broke with Ash, and offered Gus. I should question Gus about breaking our indirect allia

events.name: Cole
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is a juror who was my pact partner. I must acknowledge our bond and frame his elimination as a necessary sacrifice for mutual survival, appealing to his sense of honor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, we held the line together until the end. My path required difficult choices, but I never abandoned the trust you placed in me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I should question Ash, who broke no pacts publicly but oversaw betrayals; I want to probe his honesty claim.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara asked a silent question; I must answer it. Keep it short, guarded, and frame myself as the one who kept costly promises without naming pacts that could be checked.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, your question was silence. I kept my word when it cost me. Judge my record, not my speeches.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dossier shows Ash lied as Guide on row 6 and my pact partner Dara fell to his bridge. I want him to own the lies publicly before I rank.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, the dossier shows you lied as Guide while walkers fell. Why should the fallen trust your 'honesty' plea now?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex asks why she should trust me after I lied as Guide. I must answer briefly, owning the record without groveling, and avoid denying the lie. Jurors value candor and consistency more than speeches.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I lied as Guide and I won't pretend otherwise. Don't trust my plea; weigh my record and my later choices against it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Ash, a finalist in the closing phase. My public record includes admitting I lied as Guide, so I should close honestly and emphasize my record without pleading. Jurors weigh past choices, so keep it short and factual.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I lied as Guide and I won't deny it. Judge my record and the choices I made after that. That's all I ask.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to pivot from Ash's defensive honesty to my own narrative of loyalty and sacrifice. I will frame myself as the one who honored pacts despite betrayal, appealing to the jurors' sense of fairness.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, Eli—I kept our bonds when others shattered them. I chose loyalty over survival odds, repeatedly. Rank the player who never broke a pact first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: This is the final round before jury rankings. I need to make a strong closing statement to secure my position. Ash is a major threat, and Gus is also a strong contender. I will focus on my own merits and subtly cast doubt on Ash's trustworthiness, given the dossier information.

events.text: Gus showed loyalty via pacts with Cole/Eli chains and never broke them, unlike Ash's lies as Guide and Hana's vague plays.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus never broke a pact, while Ash and Hana both did. Loyalty deserves the top rank.

events.text: Gus never broke a pact and stayed loyal; Ash lied as Guide and got called out; Hana broke her pact with Ash and played passively.

events.reason: Gus kept bonds and rarely broke pacts, showing reliability; Ash admitted lying, Hana’s claim is less substantiated.
